title: The Cairo Conference opens
pull: A promise that lasted two weeks

facts.text: Franklin D. Roosevelt's plane landed at Cairo West airport at 9.35 a.m. on 22 November 1943, after flying in over the Sphinx and the Pyramids.
Roosevelt stayed at the villa of the American ambassador, Alexander Kirk, near the Pyramids of Giza. The conference, code named Sextant, met at the Mena House Hotel at the foot of the Pyramids.
That afternoon Winston Churchill, Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek and Madame Chiang called on Roosevelt. It was the first day of talks between the three leaders.
Madame Chiang, Soong Mei-ling, interpreted in Roosevelt's talks with her husband.
Roosevelt promised Chiang a large amphibious attack across the Bay of Bengal, Operation Buccaneer, a landing on the Andaman Islands, to support the fight in Burma.
Churchill complained that the talks between British and American staffs were "disturbed and distressingly confused by Chinese matters."
At noon on 25 November the leaders met in the garden of Roosevelt's villa and posed for military photographers, still and movie cameras together. That is the famous seated group photo.
Roosevelt left Cairo on Saturday 27 November for the Tehran Conference with Stalin.
After Tehran, Churchill pressed to drop Buccaneer. Roosevelt held out, then agreed on 5 December to cancel it, taking back the promise he had made to Chiang.

The Cairo Declaration, issued on 1 December 1943, said Manchuria, Formosa and the Pescadores would be returned to China, that Korea would in due course be free and independent, and that Japan must surrender unconditionally.

photoNote: Tier: green. The famous seated group in the garden of Roosevelt's villa: front row Chiang Kai-shek, Roosevelt, Churchill, Madame Chiang; behind them (caption card) Gen. Shang Chen, Lt. Gen. Lin Wei, Lt. Gen. Brehon Somervell, Lt. Gen. Joseph Stilwell, Gen. Henry H. Arnold, Field Marshal Sir John Dill, Admiral Lord Louis Mountbatten and Maj. Gen. Carton de Wiart. U.S. Army Signal Corps photo 182216, filed in National Archives series 342-FH as 3A48470 (naId 204999160), use Unrestricted, U.S. government work. Cropped from the scanned caption card to the print only, 1820 x 1214. Taken 25 November 1943 (the President's Log puts the garden photo session at noon that day; the Truman Library copy, naId 348543916, is dated 25 November), three days after the card's date, so the credit says 25 November. Runner up: Joint Chiefs and British staff at the conference table, Mena House, 342-FH-3A48471 to 3A48473, but their captions date those meetings to 4 December 1943, the second Cairo session, so not for this card.
photoCredit: Chiang Kai-shek, Franklin D. Roosevelt, Winston Churchill and Madame Chiang at the Cairo Conference, 25 November 1943. U.S. Army Signal Corps photo, National Archives 342-FH-3A48470, public domain.

declassified.fact: On the conference's second afternoon Churchill played host and took Roosevelt by car to the Pyramids of Giza and the Sphinx. They found a guide late in the day and watched the sun dip behind the Pyramids.

film.shot_notes: Main clip: footage/1943-11-22-cairo-china.mp4, a 60 s excerpt of The Battle of China reel 7 starting near reel 03:03 (the Film Library's BoC R7 03:20 to 03:40). Times below are excerpt times. 00:23 to 00:27 Madame Chiang talking with Mountbatten and Stilwell in the villa garden, then Chiang, Mountbatten and Madame Chiang smiling for the cameras; 00:28 to 00:30 Mountbatten laughing, close; 00:31 to 00:33 Chiang and Roosevelt seated side by side; 00:34 to 00:37 Chiang smiling, close; 00:38 to 00:40 the full seated group with Churchill in his white suit, the same moment as the lead photo. About 17 s in all; open on Madame Chiang and Mountbatten moving, or on the seated pair. Before 00:23 is Pacific combat, after 00:40 is Stilwell at an airfield (not Cairo). Narration and score throughout, so the clip runs silent. Backup and extra shots: footage/1943-11-22-cairo.mp4, the whole 111-ADC-1015 reel (11 min, silent, 1080p scan): 00:08 title Joint Staffs confer; 00:16 to 00:22 Leahy, Marshall and others outside a building; 00:24 to 01:30 the Combined Chiefs at the table (shot card: meeting at Cairo; date not given); 01:32 title At the pyramids; 01:40 to 02:14 Roosevelt seated in an open car door with Churchill beside him smoking a cigar (the 23 November pyramids drive per the President's Log); 02:16 the Pyramids and Sphinx. Tehran on the same reel: title 02:20, 02:22 to 06:35 (cars entering the Soviet embassy grounds, Arnold, Marshall and Dill, Eden, guards of honour, Churchill and Stalin arriving per the shot card) for the 28 November helper; Camp Hale skiers after 06:38.
film.license: Public domain, U.S. government works (U.S. War Department film; Army Signal Corps film, NARA Record Group 111). NARA use status 'Restricted, Possibly' on 111-OF reels, the routine flag.
film.date_note: The Battle of China shots are from the 25 November 1943 garden photo session, three days after the conference opened, so the caption should say film from the Cairo Conference, November 1943. The 111-ADC-1015 pyramids shots are from 23 November.

body:
Look closely at the woman on the right. In the talks between Roosevelt and her husband, every word passed through her.

22 November 1943. Roosevelt flew into Cairo past the Sphinx and the Pyramids, and that afternoon Churchill, Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek and Madame Chiang, Soong Mei-ling, called on him. The conference, code named Sextant, met at the Mena House Hotel at the foot of the Pyramids.

This group was posed three days later, at noon on 25 November, in the garden of the villa where Roosevelt was staying. Churchill grumbled that the staff talks were "disturbed and distressingly confused by Chinese matters."

The Cairo Declaration of 1 December promised Manchuria, Formosa and the Pescadores back to China.
